listenings.text: Luiz, it's Paulo Rezende. You asked me about the tariff at the dinner, so here is my honest answer. If they approved it tomorrow, nothing would change until planting, and planting is four months away. If it reached my customers at all, it would reach them at harvest, six months after that. So if I were you, I would not answer that question at the table. I would ask them who would have to change what, and by when.

Luiz, Megan. The visitors on Tuesday will ask you about the tariff. Do not take a side. If you took one, it would end up in a note that somebody sends to head office, and you would spend a week explaining it. If they push, give them the timeline: the decision, then planting, then harvest. If I were in the room, I would say one more thing. Tell them what you would do differently if the decision went the other way. That is what they came for.
